posts.text: He was feeling puss that day https://t.co/khJPkCZAFE

🚨🇺🇸🇮🇷 I spent today on calls with sources on both sides of this war... Trump came within one last-minute "no" of restarting it

Here's the rest of what they told me...

Trump sat in the Situation Room two days running with strikes fully staged.

Embassies were packing, Iraq closed its airspace, even Cyprus was calling around.

He walked out and said NOT YET.

The White House is now three camps: Rubio and Bessent want the blockade and the status quo, Vance and Witkoff want a deal, and CENTCOM's commander leads the finish-it camp, which is losing its pull. 

Swapping Susie Wiles for Stephen Miller, who pitched the job on winding the war down, is one of the clearest signs yet.

The talks were the real story. This morning Bloomberg had a breakthrough close.

By afternoon, two sources on opposite sides of the table told me within ten minutes of each other that it had collapsed.

The Qataris are furious at Iranian stubbornness, and the sticking point is sequencing: sanctions can come back tomorrow, but uranium shipped abroad and inspectors inside bombed sites can't be undone, so Tehran won't move first.

Make no mistake, Trump calls the shots here, not Netanyahu... and today he stepped back from the edge.

He'll be asked again soon... what matters is who's in the room when he is.

@WeTheBrandon

🚨🇺🇸🇮🇷 Closer to a nuclear strike than any time since the Cuban Missile Crisis... that’s the read from two veterans watching Iran hand out iodine pills

Matthew Hoh, the former Marine and State Department official, says every nuclear scare of the last 80 years was an accident or a misread, and this is the first since 1962 where the use would be planned.

Karen Kwiatkowski, a retired Air Force lieutenant colonel, points out Trump was still talking about destroying “what’s left of the country” after the midterms, so Tehran’s precautions aren’t paranoia.

Both put odds of a deal at 3 out of 10, and both see one brake neither side controls: Eizenkot.

Karen says he ran against Netanyahu to save an exhausted IDF, which means pulling back from Syria and Lebanon and cooling it on Iran.

So the question for this weekend is whether Washington reads Israel’s turn inward the same way... as the exit it’s been looking for.

@MatthewPHOH @karen4the6th @wethebrandon

posts.text:
🚨🇺🇸🇮🇷 Who’s still out there? Navy destroyers have been parked off Iran for 10 months with no finish line, and the carrier meant to relieve them is sitting in Singapore

Bobby Jones, a retired destroyer officer, says the escorts that stayed behind when the Lincoln went home are now at month 10 or 11, maintenance cycles are stacked on top of each other, and a Pacific carrier group had to be pulled in because nothing else was ready.

The Roosevelt now taking a port call in Singapore tells him the strike window just got pushed.

Bobby’s point is that nobody on either side has a plan past the blockade.

Iran has shown real restraint, Washington is playing tit-for-tat because it doesn’t know what else to do, and the two things America wants most, inspectors inside Pickaxe Mountain and open shipping, run into one wall: inspectors can’t be un-let-in, sanctions can be flipped back on in a second, and Tehran knows it.

His bottom line: there will be a toll on Hormuz, Pakistan and Qatar will broker it, and the crews on those ships will be the last to hear.

@WeTheBrandon

CHUCK SCHUMER EMAILS WITH OPEC SHOW DEMOCRATS COORDINATED GAS PRICE SPIKES TO BLAME TRUMP
By Jonathan Gregory

Washington, DC - November 6, 2026
Emails uncovered by the district attorney show Chuck Schumer and Democratic senators coordinating with OPEC leaders to force gas prices higher into the election. The messages describe a plan to keep prices elevated through the final months so voters would associate the increases with Trump. Once the election ended the contacts would reverse and prices would return to normal levels. The strategy relied on the public never seeing the direct communications that timed the spikes.

Highs in gas prices during the last few months match the timeline in the released emails. The coordinated pressure on OPEC created artificial increases that Democrats then used to attack Trump’s record. Officials who participated expected the election outcome to allow an immediate reversal. The plan failed to account for Trump remaining in power and the continued high prices that never dropped on schedule. The district attorney’s documents now place the full sequence of contacts into public view.

The obvious play by the Democrats has been exposed as a deliberate effort to make Trump look bad at the pump. Gas prices were treated as a campaign weapon rather than a market result. The emails confirm the intent to maintain the elevated levels only until the votes were cast. Americans who paid more during those months deserve the complete records released without delay. The coordination stands documented and the planned return to normal never arrived under the timeline they set.
